features.note: Twin green shell vessels + finned motor and cylindrical screw compressor on top + control cabinet = unmistakable water-cooled screw chiller silhouette.
Evaporator/condenser barrels have bolted flange rings, dished heads, saddles and a nameplate; proportions match ~380 TR class.

Copper discharge line runs compressor-to-condenser with plausible elbows; red condenser-water risers terminate in upward flanges (tower connection). Copper line enters the shell without a visible flange/joint.
Green painted-steel vessels with correct specular rolloff, dark brushed-metal compressor, copper pipe, emissive HMI screen and status LED all read as intended PBR.

defects: Copper discharge pipe meets the condenser shell with no flange, weld collar or nozzle transition — reads as intersecting geometry at the joint.
Red condenser-water risers crowd behind the compressor at top-right; their lower run into the shell is hidden, so the water circuit cannot be fully traced from this angle.
Floor plane is featureless dark grey; the equipment floats visually with only a faint contact shadow.
corrections: Add a flange disc or weld collar where the copper discharge pipe enters the condenser shell.
Offset the two red risers ~0.3 m toward the camera-right so their entry nozzles into the condenser barrel are visible.
Add a subtle grid or concrete tint to the ground plane to anchor the skid.

mechanical.note: probe.mjs medians via SwiftShader: 221 draws / 71,264 tris — under every HANDBOOK device budget (strictest tier: ~300-500 draws, 300-500k tris). fps=0 is a SwiftShader/probe sampling artifact (only 9 frames sampled), not a scene failure. console_clean inferred from clean load + successful render in probe and capture; neither harness actually records console messages (tooling gap). No design-spec.yaml exists for this pre-skill design: thresholds assumed as global_min=0.75, per-feature=0.70 for this smoke test.
